statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-88092 (GHSA-rv87-ccxw-8ggf) is an ASP.NET Core security feature bypass in Kestrel: an aborted HTTP/1 connection can reparse unread request-body bytes as another request, opening a request-smuggling or desynchronization path. Microsoft lists the ASP.NET Core 10.0 runtime packs, including linux-musl-x64 and linux-musl-arm64, as affected from 10.0.0 through 10.0.12 and fixed in 10.0.13, on Windows, Linux and macOS (https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-rv87-ccxw-8ggf, https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/472, https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/10.0/10.0.13/10.0.13.md). DHI dotnet10-runtime for Alpine 3.23 builds .NET 10 for Linux from Microsoft's source release, and each build's version is the .NET runtime version it carries. Scanned all 264 packages of the twelve published builds (10.0.2-r0 through 10.0.10-r0, 10.0.13-r0, 10.0.14-r0 and 10.0.15-r0) for x86_64 and aarch64, including the debug packages and the files inside the nupkg, zip and tar.gz archives they hold. Implementation copies of Microsoft.AspNetCore.Server.Kestrel.Core.dll are in the Microsoft.AspNetCore.App shared framework (aspnetcore10-runtime, and the .NET SDK held by dotnet10-runtime-bootstrap) and in the ASP.NET Core runtime pack and runtime archive in dotnet10-runtime-bootstrap. Every implementation copy carries the build's own .NET version: 10.0.2 to 10.0.10 in the first nine builds, which are unfixed, and 10.0.13 or later from 10.0.13-r0 on; the other copies are reference assemblies with no implementation code. The fix is dotnet/dotnet commit 34ac57b7d95c2d9e34f072b04d3bf06e7fb0bf64 on release/10.0.1xx ("Stop the HTTP/1 request loop when the connection is aborted"), which changes Kestrel's HTTP/1 connection handling; it is in the v10.0.113 source tag and not in v10.0.112 (https://github.com/dotnet/dotnet/commit/34ac57b7d95c2d9e34f072b04d3bf06e7fb0bf64). Every implementation copy records the dotnet/dotnet commit it was built from, and on both architectures that is the v10.0.110 tag in 10.0.10-r0 and the v10.0.113 tag in 10.0.13-r0. The range ends at 10.0.13-r0 because it is the first published build with the fix.
